subject: Recap + questionnaire: key custody, SOC 2, GDPR/HIPAA next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: security@healthix.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: encryption & key custody items from today

Hi Ethan / Healthix security team,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Per your ask, quick recap of the technical/security points we covered plus proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the procurement track.

High-level status and compliance
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type I; Type II audit is in progress with an expected completion window mid-Q3 2027. A redacted report is attached for your review.
- GDPR & HIPAA: Platform supports data processing controls for GDPR; we are willing to sign a BAA for HIPAA-covered workloads.

Encryption & key custody (summary)- At-rest: data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 (GCM where applicable).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced for all service endpoints.
- Default key model: Redwood-managed keys (hosted KMS) for standard hosted API usage.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): supported for hosted and Dedicated deployments. Options include cloud KMS integration (customer project) and HSM-backed CMK for stronger custody guarantees.
- On-prem / Private: for air-gapped or regulated deployments, we can integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11 or KMIP) and run the control plane in your VPC.

Practical considerations we discussed- Key rotation: can be customer-triggered or scheduled; when CMK is enabled, the key wrap is performed with the customer's key material (no plaintext key export).
- Latency: calling an external KMS/HSM can add ~5-10ms per request on average — we recommend a short PoC to measure in your environment.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache is still used; when wrapped keys are in use, we apply envelope encryption to the cached content to avoid exposing raw model state.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_report_v1_redacted.pdf, cmk_integration_guide.pdf

Next steps (proposed)
1) Please send your vendor security questionnaire; we will prioritize a full pass and aim to return answers within 3 business days.
2) If you’d like an architecture/tech-deep-dive, we can schedule a 60-minute session (suggest Wed/Thu next week PST).
3) We’ll prepare a filled questionnaire, redacted SOC 2 evidence, and a draft BAA for your legal team.

Are any of the proposed next steps urgent (e.g., needed for an SSO or procurement kickoff)?

Best,
Aisha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Healthix vendor questionnaire — need technical + compliance answers

Aisha / Marissa — draft answers and technical notes below (happy to iterate):

1) BYOK / HSM-backed CMK support- Hosted (cloud) mode: we support customer-managed keys by integrating with the customer's cloud KMS (GCP KMS / AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) under the customer's project/subscription. The CMK is used to envelope-wrap the data encryption keys used by Redwood; Redwood never stores the raw key material for a CMK.
- Optionally, for HSM-backed keys, customers can provision a KMS key backed by Cloud HSM (or equivalent) in their cloud project — Redwood will call the KMS APIs for sign/encrypt operations.
- Private / on-prem: we support direct HSM integration via PKCS#11 or KMIP. For customers with an on-prem HSM or partner HSM appliance, Redwood's Private control plane can be configured to call the HSM directly for key operations.

2) Key rotation and control- Rotation can be customer-initiated via KMS (recommended) or scheduled. When CMK is enabled, all envelope keys are re-wrapped with the new CMK; Redwood does not retain unobfuscated previous CMK material. We do keep audit logs of key wrap/unwrapping operations, and can surface key change events in the Console.

3) Encryption specifics- At-rest: AES-256-GCM for stored artifacts, and envelope encryption with CMK when enabled.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+; mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private if you require mTLS to our endpoints.
- Cache/prefixs: cache contents are envelope-encrypted; ephemeral keys are rotated frequently to limit exposure.

4) Latency and performance tradeoffs- Calling an external KMS/HSM adds overhead; in our tests we see ~5-10ms additional latency per generation request when doing synchronous external wrap/unwrap on every call. We mitigate via:
  * Local envelope key caching with TTL, re-wrapping at configured intervals
  * Batch wrapping for multi-request operations where applicable
We recommend a short PoC to measure impact against your traffic pattern.

5) Auditability & logs- Audit logs for key operations (wrap/unwrap/rotate) are available and can be shipped to your logging endpoint (Cloud Logging / S3 / SIEM). We can include redacted samples in the SOC evidence packet.

6) HIPAA/BAA- Separate from pure key mechanics: we support BAAs and will include the draft in the package.

Open items / caveats- For streamed KV/cache encryption in high-throughput inference paths, there are edge cases where envelope key expiry can cause transient re-wrapping; we'll flag these during PoC and propose configuration knobs.
- For customers expecting sub-ms per-token SLOs at high QPS with external HSMs, Dedicated/private topologies (local HSM or colocated KMS) will be necessary to avoid repeated network hops.

Proposed next step: 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security team to walk through PKCS#11 options and run through a short PoC plan. Draft agenda below:
1) Key lifecycle architecture and flow diagrams (20m)
2) Integration options (cloud KMS, Cloud HSM, PKCS#11/KMIP) (15m)
3) Performance/latency impact and cache modes (15m)
4) Q&A and PoC scoping (10m)

I can join the call Wed 24th 10:00-11:30 PST or Thu 25th 08:00-12:00 PST — tell me which slot works.
